payload.body:
Before people know you well, they often get a clear sense of what you like. It shows up in what you wear, how you arrange your home, what you order, and the things you choose to keep around you.

You usually know when something appeals to you. A place feels right, you like the way something looks, or a person immediately catches your attention. Your preferences tend to become visible because they keep showing up in the choices you make.

Other people usually respond to this. They notice your style, find you attractive, compliment the choices you make, or start associating you with a certain look or way of carrying yourself. That response can feel good without needing to become the reason you keep choosing the same thing.

Being wanted and wanting the choice yourself are different experiences. Someone can find you attractive without being someone you would choose. Something can look perfect on you and still stop feeling like you. Other people's approval can tell you what they respond to, but it cannot tell you what you should keep choosing.
